names.note: The nominative of the form this folder's own Russian citation prints, «Свт. Иоанна Златоустого, архиепископа Константинопольского» — a calendar lists its saints in the genitive, and the rank and the see are their own fields here.
As saint.gr's own line prints it, monotonic, without the rank: «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Χρυσόστομος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κωνσταντινούπολης».
Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 30 ianuarie, «Sfinţii Trei Ierarhi: Vasile cel Mare, Grigorie Teologul şi Ioan Gură de Aur».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 ноября ст. ст.; «Свт. Иоанна Златоустого, архиепископа Константинопольского (407)»

attestations.note: All-night vigil: «Совершается всенощное бдение». The same calendar keeps him again on 30 января ст. ст., in the Synaxis of the Ecumenical Teachers and Hierarchs — «Собор Вселенских учителей и святителей Василия Великого, Григория Богослова и Иоанна Златоустого» — which names the three of them and no one else. That is a joint commemoration and not a feast of his own, so this row stands on his own day and the second day is recorded here; the saint is not rendered on it.

source.text: Basilica, the Romanian Patriarchate’s news agency — Orthodox calendar, 13 November; “†) St. John Chrysostom, archbishop of Constantinople, and his mother, St. Anthusa”

attestations.note: Marked †) in the Patriarchate’s calendar. Also 27 and 30 January.

source.text: Ορθόδοξος Συναξαριστής (saint.gr), 13 Νοεμβρίου; «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Χρυσόστομος Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κωνσταντινούπολης»

locations.note: Died on the road while being moved to a more remote place of exile.

track.note: Born here and formed here: rhetoric under Libanius, some years as a hermit in the mountains above the city, and then the preaching that earned him his name. The year he left is the one this stay is really about — he was taken to Constantinople at the end of 397 and consecrated in February 398 — so 397 is a departure the sources do fix, unlike the null at the other end, which is birth with no month to it.

Archbishop from 398, largely against his will. The six years are drawn as one stay although they were not: he was deposed at the Synod of the Oak in 403 and recalled within days, which is too short a journey for a map to draw honestly and is in his life in words instead. The exile that stuck came the following year.

Three years of exile in Armenia Secunda, and the one place on this track the corpus did not already record — his own letters are written from here, which is as well attested as anything in his life. The site is identified with Göksun; the 25 km is that identification's own slack, not doubt about the exile.

He did not travel here to stay: he was being marched to Pityus, further off again, and died on the road on 14 September 407. So the last leg is the forced march itself, and the wide uncertainty is the corpus's own on the place of death rather than anything this track adds.

hymns.text: Din gura ta ca o lumină de foc strălucind harul, lumea a luminat. Vistieriile neiubirii de argint lumii a câștigat. Înălțimea gândului smerit nouă ne-a arătat. Iar prin cuvintele tale învățându-ne, Părinte Ioane Gură de Aur, roagă pe Cuvântul, Hristos Dumnezeu, să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — «Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Ioan Gură de Aur», glas 8, from the Tropar tab of his page for 13 noiembrie (the page sets soft hyphens inside several words for its own line-breaking; they are not letters and are not copied here)

english.text: Grace shining forth from thy mouth like a torch of fire has enlightened the world; it has won for the world the treasures of freedom from the love of money, and has shown us the height of humility of mind. Instructing us by thy words, father John Chrysostom, pray to the Word, Christ God, that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Уст твоих, якоже светлость огня возсиявши, благодать/ вселенную просвети:/ не сребролюбия мирови сокровища сниска,/ высоту нам смиренномудрия показа./ Но твоими словесы наказуя, отче Иоанне Златоусте,// моли Слова, Христа Бога, спастися душам нашим.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 января ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителя Иоанна Златоуста»

english.text: The grace that shone forth from thy lips like the brightness of fire has enlightened the whole world; it gained for the world treasures that are not those of the love of money, and showed us the height of humility of mind. But teaching us by thy words, O father John Chrysostom, entreat the Word, Christ God, that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Возвеселися таинственно честная Церковь/ возвращением честных твоих мощей,/ и, сия сокрывши, яко злато многоценное,/ поющим тя неоскудно подавает/ молитвами твоими исцелений благодать,// Иоанне Златоусте.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 января ст. ст. — «Кондак святителя Иоанна Златоуста»

english.text: The honourable Church rejoiced in a mystery at the return of thy honourable relics, and having hidden them away like gold of great price she gives without stinting, to those who sing of thee, the grace of healings by thy prayers, O John Chrysostom.

hymns.text: Яко апостолов единонравнии/ и вселенныя учителие,/ Владыку всех молите/ мир вселенней даровати// и душам нашим велию милость.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 января ст. ст. — «Тропарь святителей»

english.text: As those of one mind with the apostles and teachers of the whole world, entreat the Master of all to grant peace to the world and great mercy to our souls.

hymns.text: Священныя и боговещанныя проповедники,/ верх учителей, Господи,/ приял еси в наслаждение благих Твоих и упокоение:/ труды бо онех и смерть приял еси паче всякаго всеплодия,// Едине прославляяй святыя Твоя.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 января ст. ст. — «Кондак святителей»

english.text: The sacred and God-proclaiming preachers, the chief of teachers, thou hast received, O Lord, into the enjoyment of thy good things and into rest; for thou hast accepted their labours and their death above every whole burnt offering, O thou who alone glorifiest thy saints.
